newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysian Airline requests fare hike.
newsitem.headline: Malaysian Airline requests fare hike.

text.p: Malaysia's national carrier Malaysian Airline Systems Bhd (MAS) has proposed lifting its international air fares by three percent, the national Bernama news agency reported on Thursday.

The proposal was made to the government after the International Air Transport Association (IATA) recommended a rise in air fares worldwide due to the steady rise in jet fuel prices over several years, Bernama quoted MAS chairman Tajudin Ramli as saying on Thursday.
Tajudin claimed that since over 230 airlines around the world had roposed fare hikes of up to 10 percent the request was fair, Bernama reported.
Malaysia's Transport Minister Ling Liong Sik said on Wednesday that MAS was free to raise its international fares given that the government only controlled domestic air fares.

The share of jet fuel costs, which made up slightly over 10 per cent of MAS's total expenditure last year, had risen to 14.6 percent within the first six months of this year due to the price increase, Ramli said.
Around 65 per cent of the fuel was consumed by MAS aircraft serving international flights, he said.
